acceptance: No create-github-app-token step uses app-id in either repository, and the deprecation warning is gone from their runs.
theseus infra setup delivers the review App client ID, and a re-run plans no change.
A review run, a gate run and a SQLGlot delivery run succeed after the switch.
description:
actions/create-github-app-token deprecates the `app-id` input in favor of `client-id`. Uses on 2026-11-20: Theseus main .github/workflows/gate.yml:259 and :420 and review.yml:231, :535 and :547 (secrets.REVIEW_APP_ID); BenchBox develop .github/workflows/site-inputs.yml:131 (SITE_BRIDGE_APP_ID) and sqlglot-delivery.yml:239 and :298 (SQLGLOT_DELIVERY_APP_ID). Each App's client ID must be stored (secret or variable) before switching, and `theseus infra setup` should deliver the review App's client ID the same way it delivers REVIEW_APP_ID today. Changes to the review workflows are soundness paths and follow the review gate rules.

Decision gate: before editing workflows, confirm each App's client ID is stored where the workflow will read it (secret or variable, as the owner chooses), and that `theseus infra setup` can deliver the review App's client ID. If storing it needs an owner console action, ask first.
Verification rubric: a run of each changed workflow (BenchBox review-verdict, review-gate, site-inputs, sqlglot-delivery; Theseus gate and review) succeeds after the switch and shows no `app-id` deprecation warning. A second `theseus infra setup` plans nothing.
Guardrails: never print or log a client ID together with a private key. Theseus's change ships through a release and lock promotion like any other workflow change. BenchBox's review workflow callers change only through that promotion, never by hand-editing the pinned reusable workflows.
